predecessors.name: Jōmon period
predecessors.text: Kyushu, Shikoku and Honshu south of northern Tohoku, the part of the Jomon country that the jomon-period dossier hands to the Yayoi at 300 BCE

successors.name: Yamato
successors.text: the Nara Basin, where the Yamato Kingship 'is usually believed to have begun c.

ledger.x: 300 BCE: the Yayoi culture replaces the Jomon in Kyushu, Shikoku and southern Honshu.
AD 300: the Yayoi period ends and the Kofun period begins ('an era in the history of Japan from about 300 to 538 AD').
AD 300: the Yayoi period gives way to the Kofun period under the Yamato Kingship.

certainty.note: No treaty, survey or administrative record fixes any Yayoi frontier; the extent is the researcher's reading of a prehistoric culture's range, and the northern edge (Epi-Jomon) is approximate.
